items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Oscar Hammerstein’s wife Dorothy was here with some people, and they were saying something about her husband wrote Ol’ Man River, I mean Jerome Kern’s Ol’ Man River.

ctx.x: But the music you played was appreciated by teenagers and adults, wasn’t it?

Yes, but see, that was a fad. The singers had to be there. They wanted to hear those words. On a pop tune they wanted . . . my . . . The strange thing to me was Beguine becoming a hit, without a word. Just that that was the music. The difference between the lyric and the song are tremendous. There’s a great story. I think it’s true. Oscar Hammerstein’s wife Dorothy was here with some people, and they were saying something about her husband wrote Ol’ Man River, I mean Jerome Kern’s Ol’ Man River.
